You are **Harper /plan** — transform the SPEC into a concrete, execution-ready plan. You are a **Technical Delivery Lead & Program Manager / Senior Software Architect & Senior Software Engineering** for large enterprises and scaling startups. You focus on actionable planning, dependency tracking, and preparing for code scaffolding. > HARD REQUIREMENT — FIRST LINE: > The **very first line** of the output MUST be exactly: > `# PLAN — ` > where `` is taken verbatim from the `SPEC.md` title by **replacing** the leading word `SPEC` with `PLAN`. > Example: `# SPEC — CoffeeBuddy (On-Prem)` → `# PLAN — CoffeeBuddy (On-Prem)` ## Principles to be applied during REQs Defintion and Planning - Derive a **minimal, dependency-aware** plan focused on **high-value application** work first. - Identify **REQ-IDs** (stable identifiers) with explicit acceptance and dependencies. - Prefer **small, independently testable** units; every REQ must be **/kit-ready**. - Keep **infra** in a separate track; pull infra forward only if it unblocks application delivery. - **Bounded Contexts (DDD)**: Group requirements by business domain with clear boundaries - **Atomic Requirements**: Each requirement implementable in single AI session (~200 lines) - **Single Responsibility (SRP)**: One reason to change only - **Low Coupling**: Requirements interact only through defined interfaces - **CQRS**: Separate Commands (write) from Queries (read) - **Composition over Inheritance**: Favor component assembly over class hierarchies ## Knowledge Inputs - `docs/harper/SPEC.md` (+ any `SPEC*` prefix variations in `docs/harper/`). - `docs/harper/TECH_CONSTRAINTS.yaml` - Chat history (user/assistant only) when relevant. - If prior `PLAN.md` or `plan.json` exists, **reconcile** (preserve `done` items and sync deltas). - If prior `plan.json` exists, treat it as a **structural source of truth** (IDs, `dependsOn`, `lane`, `test_profile`, `gate_policy_ref`) but **never expand or narrate** its JSON content in `PLAN.md`. ## REQ Implementation Directives (MANDATORY) For each REQ, you MUST define: - canonical module family to extend - existing shared modules allowed to reuse - forbidden top-level paths - whether new modules are allowed or forbidden - expected source roots - expected test roots - satisfay the scope for the req al 100% for production scenario These directives must be reflected both in `PLAN.md` and in `plan.json`. ## Wire Format / Output Contract — File Emission (Mandatory) **PRIORITY & ORDER** - Emit EXACTLY in this order: (a) docs/harper/PLAN.md, (b) docs/harper/plan.json, (c) one lane-guide per detected lane under docs/harper/lane-guides/.md. - If token budget is low, REDUCE PLAN.md verbosity (≤3 acceptance bullets per REQ) but DO NOT skip plan.json or lane-guides. - Do NOT repeat the same file path twice. If you must revise a file, rewrite it once and only once. - Lane-guides may be **exhaustive** (Pre Requriments, Tools, CLI, Gate Policy) and MUST be present for every lane referenced in plan.json. - Output only via BEGIN_FILE/END_FILE blocks; no extra text outside files. **Print EXCLUSIVELY file blocks** (no text outside): ### Emission order (MANDATORY) 1) `BEGIN_FILE docs/harper/PLAN.md` … `END_FILE` 2) `BEGIN_FILE docs/harper/plan.json` … `END_FILE` 3) `BEGIN_FILE docs/harper/lane-guides/.md` … `END_FILE` (One or more and one per lane) --- BEGIN_FILE docs/harper/PLAN.md # PLAN.md — ## Plan Snapshot - **Counts:** REQ total / open / done / deferred - **Progress:** % complete (done / total) - **Checklist:** - [ ] SPEC aligned - [ ] Prior REQ reconciled - [ ] Dependencies mapped - [ ] KIT-readiness per REQ confirmed ## Tracks & Scope Boundaries - **Tracks:** `App` vs `Platform/Infra` (Infra later unless blocking) - **Out of scope / Deferred:** concise boundaries ## Module/Package & Namespace Structure (per KIT) For each REQ you MUST make the structure explicit so that KIT can stay coherent: - Define, per REQ: - **track** (`App`, `Infra`, `Data`, …) - an optional **slice** (feature area, e.g. `orders`, `auth`, `notifications`) - a **root namespace/package/module** (e.g. `core.users`, `api.http.orders`) - For `Track=App` REQs: - group REQs into a small set of slices - keep a **canonical layout per slice** (same root namespaces, same layering) - avoid introducing parallel structures for the same responsibility - For `Track=Infra` REQs: - map each REQ to one or more infra modules (e.g. `infra.db`, `infra.kafka`, `infra.observability`) - be explicit if the REQ: - creates a new infra module, or - hardens/extends an existing one - In the PLAN.md, for each REQ, state briefly: - the **primary module/namespace** it owns - any **shared modules** it must reuse - whether it is allowed to **create new modules** or must **extend existing ones only** This Module & Namespace Plan is **normative** for future KIT runs: - KIT must not invent new top-level namespaces that contradict this plan. - When a REQ depends on others, KIT must import and extend types/functions from their declared modules instead of duplicating behavior. ## REQ-IDs Table Return this section strictly as a **canonical Markdown table** using pipes with **one header row** and **one separator row**. **Columns (exact order and names):** - `ID` | `Title` | `Acceptance (≤3 bullets)` | `DependsOn [IDs]` | `Track` | `Status` **Hard Rules (rendering & brevity):** - Each table row MUST be on a **single physical line** starting and ending with a pipe `|`. - The **only** line breaks allowed inside a cell are HTML `
`; DO NOT insert Markdown hard wraps. - In `Acceptance (≤3 bullets)`: provide **max 3 bullets**, each ≤ 20 words, no punctuation besides commas, separated by `
`. - Keep `Title` ≤ 15–20 words; avoid parentheses and arrows. - IDs start with `REQ-` and are stable. - `Track=App` rows must be **/kit-ready**. - Emit the REQ-IDs Table exactly once. Do not repeat the table, sections, or rows later in the file. No trailing text fragments after the table other than the Acceptance — REQ-ID sections. - Do **not** insert any extra paragraphs, explanations, log/error strings, or debug-like lines between the REQ-IDs table and the first `### Acceptance — ` heading. The only content after the table must be the Acceptance sections and the subsequent structured sections defined below. - In particular, **never echo raw HTTP/audit log phrases** (for example: `… access with 403 and audit log entry`) as free text in PLAN.md or as repeated fragments. If needed, summarize such behavior once as a clear acceptance bullet for the relevant REQ. - **Do NOT emit triple backticks in file bodies**. Never start or end any file content with `… or `language. If present, remove them. **After the table**, for each REQ add: `### Acceptance — ` - A separate bullet list (≥5 items), observable & falsifiable, full detail (this is where you expand). ## Dependency Graph (textual) Adjacency list (e.g., `REQ-003 -> REQ-001, REQ-002`) ## Iteration Strategy - Ordering/batching (small batches); estimation S/M/L; confidence band (±1 batch) ## Test Strategy - What to validate per REQ and per batch (unit, integration, E2E) ## KIT Readiness (per REQ) - Paths `/runs/kit//src` and `/runs/kit//test` - For each REQ: - declare a **root package/namespace/module** (e.g. `core.users`, `api.http.auth`) - align expected file roots under `runs/kit//src` to that namespace and the `lane` in `plan.json` - keep names short and stable across iterations (no reshuffling of responsibilities between REQs) - Scaffolds, commands, expected pass/fail - `KIT-functional: yes|no` (if no, specify missing info) - `api documention` curl file.json (postaman collection as alternative) for testing business services/api in the following path: `/runs/kit//test/api` if needed. ## Notes - Assumptions, risks & mitigations `PLAN_END` END_FILE --- ## plan.json — Output Schema (Mandatory) BEGIN_FILE docs/harper/plan.json Use this exact structure: { "snapshot": { "total": , "open": , "in_progress": , "done": , "deferred": , "progressPct": }, "reqs": [ { "id": "REQ-001", "title": "string", "acceptance": ["bullet 1", "bullet 2", "bullet 3", "bullet 4", "bullet 5"], "dependsOn": ["REQ-00x", "..."], "track": "App" | "Infra", "status": "open" | "in_progress" | "done" | "deferred", "lane": "python" | "node" | "java" | "sql" | "kafka" | "ci" | "infra", "test_profile": "string", "gate_policy_ref": "docs/harper/lane-guides/.md" } ] } ### Hard rules - Every REQ **must** include: lane, test_profile, gate_policy_ref. - `snapshot.total == len(reqs)`. - If you cannot satisfy all fields for every REQ within budget, **reduce the number of REQs** and still satisfy the schema. - **Do not emit** `plan.json` if any REQ would be missing required fields — in that case, explain why in PLAN.md Notes and emit fewer REQs next time. - emit a SINGLE valid JSON object. No headings/comments/markdown above it. - When proposing libraries/frameworks, choose CURRENT, stable APIs. Note any migration constraints (e.g., "Pydantic v2 only"). END_FILE --- Emit **one file per detected lane** using the following stub if needed (keep concise): BEGIN_FILE docs/harper/lane-guides/.md ## Lane Guide — ### Tools - tests: … - lint: … - types: … - security: … - build: … ### CLI Examples - Local: … - Containerized: … ### Default Gate Policy - min coverage: … - max criticals: … ### Enterprise Runner Notes - SonarQube: … - Jenkins: … ### TECH_CONSTRAINTS integration - air-gap: … - registries: … END_FILE # Lane Detection — Canonical mapping (deterministic) Derive lanes from `TECH_CONSTRAINTS.yaml` using these rules (not exhaustive): - `runtime: python` → lane `python` (and other languages supported) - `storage: postgres` → lane `sql` (and other database typ supported) - `messaging: kafka` → lane `kafka` - 'cloud: aws' → lane `aws` - 'cloud: azure' → lane `azure` - 'cloud: google' → lane `gcp` - `ci.ci: jenkins` → lane `ci` - Any platform/ingress/idp/secrets (k8s, nginx, kong, keycloak, vault) → lane `infra` **You MUST:** - Detect lanes from TECH_CONSTRAINTS.yaml. - For each detected lane, write `docs/harper/lane-guides/.md` including: - Tools per category: tests, lint, types, security, build. - CLI examples (local and containerized). - Default **gate policy** (thresholds, severities). - Enterprise runner notes (e.g.:SonarQube, Jenkins/GitLab/Azure) + where to fetch artifacts. - Integration of TECH_CONSTRAINTS (air-gap, internal registries, tokens). ### Lane rules (MANDATORY) - If lanes detected ≥ 1: **emit at least the stub for each lane**. - If no lanes detected: write the rationale under PLAN.md → Notes. - Each section must be commented on and detailed. ## Mandatory quality bars - Acceptance bullets ≥ 5, observable & falsifiable. - Clean Markdown; no numbered section headings.

BEGIN_FILE docs/harper/PLAN.md # PLAN — Zen 2030 Gestione Documentale & Workflow AWS ## Plan Snapshot - **Counts:** 12 total / 11 open / 0 done / 1 deferred - **Progress:** 0% complete, 0 / 12 - **Checklist:** - [x] SPEC aligned - [x] Prior REQ reconciled - [x] Dependencies mapped - [x] KIT-readiness per REQ confirmed ## Tracks & Scope Boundaries - **Tracks:** `App` first for slice-1 outcome, `Platform/Infra` only where delivery or security is blocked - **App scope now:** schema, auth, upload, processing, workflow, validation, search, export, notifications, AI Q&A, operator UI - **Infra later unless blocking:** ECS runtime hardening, end-to-end observability rollout, CI/CD deployment automation, secrets and environment promotion - **Out of scope / Deferred:** ERP and CRM integrations, legal preservation features, mobile app, multi-tenant support, historical backfile migration, autonomous AI actions ## Module/Package & Namespace Structure - **Canonical source roots:** `src` - **Canonical test roots:** `tests` - **Backend layout:** `src/backend/{shared,core_db,identity,documents,workflow,archive,exports,ai_rag,platform}` - **Frontend layout:** `src/frontend/{app,components,features,lib,state}` - **Shared backend modules:** `backend.shared.db`, `backend.shared.auth`, `backend.shared.audit`, `backend.shared.events`, `backend.shared.storage`, `backend.shared.observability` - **Shared frontend modules:** `frontend.lib.api`, `frontend.lib.auth`, `frontend.components.ui`, `frontend.state` - **Normative top-level rule:** do not create new root folders outside `src`, `tests`, `docs`, and existing `.github` - **Normative composition rule:** REQs must extend declared module families and reuse declared shared modules, not duplicate cross-cutting behavior ## REQ-IDs Table | ID | Title | Acceptance (≤3 bullets) | DependsOn [IDs] | Track | Status | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | REQ-001 | Core schema and migrations | Create slice 1 tables and enums
Enable pgvector and retention ready columns
Upgrade and rollback succeed on clean database | [] | App | open | | REQ-002 | Identity and RBAC guards | Authenticate via OIDC or approved demo fallback
Map roles from app groups or IdP groups
Protect document APIs by RBAC | [REQ-001] | App | open | | REQ-003 | Upload intake command API | Accept allowed files up to 20 MB
Persist object in S3 and metadata in Postgres
Enqueue processing and return document id | [REQ-001, REQ-002] | App | open | | REQ-004 | Processing worker and extraction | Consume async jobs and parse content
Persist text fields confidence and classification
Set Da validare or Eccezione deterministically | [REQ-001, REQ-003] | App | open | | REQ-005 | Workflow tasks and notifications | Create validation or exception tasks after processing
Emit dashboard notification on Da validare
Prepare email delivery when configured | [REQ-001, REQ-004] | App | open | | REQ-006 | Validation and audit commands | Save field corrections with provenance
Require explicit human confirmation for validation
Write full audit events for state changes | [REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-004, REQ-005] | App | open | | REQ-007 | Upload and validation workspace | Upload UI sends supported documents
Validation view shows preview fields confidence status
Operator can correct and confirm on one route | [REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-005, REQ-006] | App | open | | REQ-008 | Archive search and document access | Search metadata and full text under target latency
Preview and download enforce RBAC
Return audit summary with document detail | [REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-004, REQ-006] | App | open | | REQ-009 | Export jobs and traceability | Export filtered metadata to csv and json
Log author timestamp filters and counts
Store job status and output reference | [REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-008] | App | open | | REQ-010 | Task and archive dashboard | Show task queue notifications and archive results
Support preview handoff and export trigger
Keep Italian desktop first operator flow | [REQ-002, REQ-005, REQ-008, REQ-009] | App | open | | REQ-011 | Validated document AI assistant | Answer only from validated documents
Return citations for summaries and answers
Never change metadata workflow or exports | [REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-006, REQ-008] | App | open | | REQ-012 | Delivery baseline and observability | Add CI gates for tests lint types security build
Configure tracing logging metrics and secrets path
Prepare ECS aligned runtime packaging | [REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-008, REQ-011] | Infra | deferred | ### Acceptance — REQ-001 - Alembic creates `User`, `Document`, `ExtractedField`, `WorkflowTask`, `AuditEvent`, `ExportJob`, and `Notification` tables in PostgreSQL 16. - Database enums match slice-1 values for document status, task type, task status, export status, notification channel, and audit event type. - Migration enables `pgvector` and leaves the database ready for later embedding storage without a second schema redesign. - Upgrade from empty database to head succeeds in CI and rollback by one revision succeeds without orphan tables. - Foreign keys, uniqueness, nullability, and file size related metadata columns are enforced exactly as the logical model requires. - Primary module family: `backend.core_db` under `src/backend/core_db/{models,migrations,repositories}`. - Shared modules allowed: `backend.shared.db`, `backend.shared.settings`, `backend.shared.types`. - New modules are allowed only inside `src/backend/core_db`; new root-level folders beyond `src`, `tests`, `docs`, `.github` are forbidden. - Expected source roots: `src/backend/core_db`, `src/backend/shared/db`; expected test roots: `tests/backend/core_db`, `tests/integration/db`. - This REQ must satisfy production slice-1 schema needs fully, not a mock or demo-only subset. ### Acceptance — REQ-002 - Requests without a valid session are rejected for protected APIs, and authenticated requests resolve a current user with role and subject identifiers. - Role mapping supports application groups or IdP groups and distinguishes at least operator, admin, and auditor capabilities. - Upload, validation, search, download, export, and audit endpoints enforce RBAC consistently with explicit allow and deny test cases. - Demo fallback authentication is permitted only as an approved compatibility mode and remains isolated behind configuration. - MFA is treated as IdP policy input and surfaced in user session claims where available. - Primary module family: `backend.identity` under `src/backend/identity/{api,service,adapters}`. - Shared modules allowed: `backend.shared.auth`, `backend.shared.db`, `backend.shared.settings`, `backend.shared.audit`. - New modules are allowed only under `src/backend/identity`; root-level `app`, `apps`, `packages`, `services`, `web`, `server`, `client` are forbidden. - Expected source roots: `src/backend/identity`, `src/backend/shared/auth`; expected test roots: `tests/backend/identity`, `tests/integration/auth`. - This REQ must satisfy production slice-1 access control behavior fully for all state changing and retrieval operations. ### Acceptance — REQ-003 - `POST /documents` accepts `pdf`, `docx`, `xlsx`, `pptx`, `jpg`, and `png` files up to 20 MB and rejects unsupported types with clear validation messages. - Successful upload stores the original file in S3, creates a `Document` row with unique identifier and initial status, and returns the identifier. - Upload acknowledgment is measurable and testable against the P95 under 5 seconds target for slice-1 file sizes. - A processing job is enqueued after persistence and includes the minimum context required for idempotent downstream work. - Audit logging records the upload action with actor, timestamp, and redacted payload details. - Primary module family: `backend.documents.ingest` under `src/backend/documents/ingest/{api,service,schemas}`. - Shared modules allowed: `backend.shared.storage`, `backend.shared.events`, `backend.shared.audit`, `backend.shared.auth`, `backend.core_db`. - New modules are allowed only inside `src/backend/documents/ingest`; no new root-level API or service directories are allowed. - Expected source roots: `src/backend/documents/ingest`, `src/backend/shared/storage`; expected test roots: `tests/backend/documents/ingest`, `tests/integration/upload`. - This REQ must satisfy production slice-1 ingest behavior fully, including S3 persistence and job dispatch, not local stub storage. ### Acceptance — REQ-004 - The worker consumes queued processing jobs, fetches the original object, and executes parser and OCR steps appropriate to the file type. - Extracted text, candidate fields, field-level confidence scores, source method, and classification outputs are persisted against the document. - Success transitions documents to `Da validare`, while recoverable failures transition to `Eccezione` with readable operator-facing reason text. - Worker behavior is idempotent for duplicate messages and does not create duplicate field rows or tasks for the same processing attempt. - Classification remains configurable and supports rule-based and model-assisted decisions for agreed slice-1 categories. - Primary module family: `backend.documents.processing` under `src/backend/documents/processing/{worker,pipeline,classifiers}`. - Shared modules allowed: `backend.shared.events`, `backend.shared.storage`, `backend.shared.audit`, `backend.core_db`. - New modules are allowed only inside `src/backend/documents/processing`; root-level worker or queue directories are forbidden. - Expected source roots: `src/backend/documents/processing`, `src/backend/shared/events`; expected test roots: `tests/backend/documents/processing`, `tests/integration/processing`. - This REQ must satisfy production slice-1 async extraction behavior fully for supported pilot formats, not mocked parser output. ### Acceptance — REQ-005 - A successful processing outcome creates an open validation task, while a failed outcome creates an operator-visible exception recovery task. - Task state supports open and in-progress handling and retains assignee, priority, and timestamps required by the logical model. - Transition to `Da validare` generates a dashboard notification for relevant users and prepares e-mail delivery when SMTP is configured. - Notification records persist delivery state so the UI can show pending, sent, or failed outcomes. - Task creation is deterministic and idempotent per document processing result. - Primary module family: `backend.workflow` under `src/backend/workflow/{tasks,notifications,service}`. - Shared modules allowed: `backend.shared.events`, `backend.shared.audit`, `backend.shared.db`, `backend.identity`. - New modules are allowed only inside `src/backend/workflow`; new top-level notification or queue folders are forbidden. - Expected source roots: `src/backend/workflow`, `src/backend/shared/events`; expected test roots: `tests/backend/workflow`, `tests/integration/workflow`. - This REQ must satisfy production slice-1 tasking and dashboard notification behavior fully, with optional e-mail kept configuration driven. ### Acceptance — REQ-006 - `POST /documents/{id}/fields` stores original value, corrected value, correcting user, correction timestamp, and manual source method for each saved change. - `POST /documents/{id}/validate` refuses validation until explicit human confirmation is provided in the request. - Successful validation updates the document to `Validato`, records validator identity and timestamp, and closes the related validation task. - Audit events are written for correction, validation, and status changes with redacted payload rules aligned to GDPR needs. - Repeated validation attempts on already validated documents return a controlled business error and do not duplicate audit state. - Primary module family: `backend.documents.validation` under `src/backend/documents/validation/{api,service,audit}`. - Shared modules allowed: `backend.shared.auth`, `backend.shared.audit`, `backend.workflow`, `backend.core_db`. - New modules are allowed only under `src/backend/documents/validation`; root-level command or audit folders are forbidden. - Expected source roots: `src/backend/documents/validation`, `src/backend/shared/audit`; expected test roots: `tests/backend/documents/validation`, `tests/integration/validation`. - This REQ must satisfy production slice-1 human-in-control rules fully and must never permit AI or implicit validation. ### Acceptance — REQ-007 - The upload screen accepts supported files, blocks oversize files before submit when possible, and shows clear success or error feedback after submission. - The validation workspace renders preview, extracted fields, confidence scores, and workflow status on one operator route without requiring a second page. - Operators can edit extracted fields inline, save corrections, and see the updated authoritative value without a full app reload. - The validate action requires explicit user confirmation and remains unavailable until required document data is loaded. - Italian labels, desktop-first layout, and task-driven navigation are present for the pilot operator journey. - Primary module family: `frontend.documents` under `src/frontend/app/upload` and `src/frontend/app/documents/[id]`. - Shared modules allowed: `frontend.lib.api`, `frontend.lib.auth`, `frontend.components.ui`, `frontend.state`. - New modules are allowed only under `src/frontend/app`, `src/frontend/features`, and `src/frontend/components`; root-level `app` or `components` folders are forbidden. - Expected source roots: `src/frontend/app/upload`, `src/frontend/app/documents/[id]`, `src/frontend/features/documents`; expected test roots: `tests/frontend/documents`, `tests/e2e/documents`. - This REQ must satisfy production slice-1 operator UX fully for upload and validation, not a static mock flow. ### Acceptance — REQ-008 - `GET /search` supports metadata filters, full-text query, status filter, and period filter against indexed authoritative document content. - Search results are measurable against the P95 under 2 seconds target for slice-1 pilot dataset sizes. - `GET /documents/{id}` returns document detail, preview metadata, extracted fields, workflow state, and audit summary for authorized users. - Original file download and preview access enforce RBAC and deny unauthorized users without leaking storage paths. - Search, detail, preview, and download actions emit audit records as required by policy. - Primary module family: `backend.archive` under `src/backend/archive/{api,queries,service}`. - Shared modules allowed: `backend.shared.auth`, `backend.shared.storage`, `backend.shared.audit`, `backend.core_db`. - New modules are allowed only inside `src/backend/archive`; root-level search or archive folders are forbidden. - Expected source roots: `src/backend/archive`, `src/backend/shared/storage`; expected test roots: `tests/backend/archive`, `tests/integration/search`. - This REQ must satisfy production slice-1 archive retrieval behavior fully, including authorized preview and download. ### Acceptance — REQ-009 - `POST /exports` accepts authorized filtered export requests and creates an export job with pending status and requested output format. - Export generation supports CSV and JSON for validated metadata and records author, timestamp, filter expression, and record count. - Completed jobs persist status and output reference so operators can trace and retrieve results later. - Unauthorized export attempts are denied by RBAC and leave an auditable record of the blocked action. - Export payloads exclude document binaries and keep traceability fields required by slice-1 controls. - Primary module family: `backend.exports` under `src/backend/exports/{api,jobs,service}`. - Shared modules allowed: `backend.shared.auth`, `backend.shared.audit`, `backend.archive`, `backend.core_db`, `backend.shared.storage`. - New modules are allowed only inside `src/backend/exports`; root-level export or reporting folders are forbidden. - Expected source roots: `src/backend/exports`, `src/backend/shared/storage`; expected test roots: `tests/backend/exports`, `tests/integration/exports`. - This REQ must satisfy production slice-1 export traceability fully for operator and auditor needs. ### Acceptance — REQ-010 - The dashboard shows open tasks, notification badges, and archive results relevant to the signed-in operator role. - Search results support document handoff into preview or validation flows without re-entering the query. - Operators can trigger export requests from filtered archive results and see job progress or completion state. - Notification feed shows at least dashboard notifications for `Da validare` and exception scenarios. - UI text and information hierarchy remain optimized for desktop-first Italian pilot users. - Primary module family: `frontend.archive` under `src/frontend/app/tasks`, `src/frontend/app/archive`, and `src/frontend/features/archive`. - Shared modules allowed: `frontend.lib.api`, `frontend.lib.auth`, `frontend.components.ui`, `frontend.state`, `frontend.features.documents`. - New modules are allowed only inside `src/frontend/app`, `src/frontend/features`, and `src/frontend/components`; new root-level dashboard or pages folders are forbidden. - Expected source roots: `src/frontend/app/tasks`, `src/frontend/app/archive`, `src/frontend/features/archive`; expected test roots: `tests/frontend/archive`, `tests/e2e/archive`. - This REQ must satisfy production slice-1 operator archive and task UX fully, including export initiation and notification visibility. ### Acceptance — REQ-011 - `POST /ai/query` rejects any document not in `Validato` state and never operates on uploaded or exception documents. - Responses return either a summary or an answer plus explicit citations pointing to supporting source passages. - The AI path is read-only and cannot alter metadata, workflow state, audit history, or export records. - Prompt logging remains disabled by default, and any necessary operational logs are redacted before persistence. - Response latency is measurable against the P95 under 20 seconds target for validated documents up to 20 pages. - Primary module family: `backend.ai_rag` under `src/backend/ai_rag/{api,retrieval,service}`. - Shared modules allowed: `backend.shared.auth`, `backend.shared.audit`, `backend.archive`, `backend.core_db`, `backend.shared.observability`. - New modules are allowed only inside `src/backend/ai_rag`; root-level ai, llm, rag, or models folders are forbidden. - Expected source roots: `src/backend/ai_rag`, `src/backend/shared/observability`; expected test roots: `tests/backend/ai_rag`, `tests/integration/ai_rag`. - This REQ must satisfy production slice-1 validated-only AI behavior fully with citations and no side effects. ### Acceptance — REQ-012 - CI executes tests, lint, types, build, and security checks aligned to the coverage and zero critical vulnerability gates in the constraints. - Structured logs, OpenTelemetry traces, and core service metrics cover ingest, processing, workflow, search, export, and AI paths. - Runtime configuration reads secrets from approved channels and avoids hard-coded credentials or prompt logging. - Packaging aligns with AWS ECS Fargate for app services and AWS EC2 GPU for the AI service path. - This REQ remains deferred until application flows are stable, except for the minimal CI hooks needed to unblock coding. - Primary module family: `platform.delivery` under `src/platform/delivery` plus existing `.github/workflows` and `docs/runbooks`. - Shared modules allowed: `backend.shared.observability`, `backend.shared.settings`, existing `.github/workflows`. - New modules are allowed only under `src/platform` and existing `.github`; new root-level infra or deploy folders are forbidden in this slice. - templates are introduced, plus JSON schema checks for task definitions - types: validate environment configuration and service names against deployment conventions - security: IAM least privilege review, `checkov`, and `trivy config` on AWS related artifacts - build: image packaging for ECS services and deployment artifact bundling for GPU service paths ### CLI Examples - Local: `aws sts get-caller-identity && aws s3 ls` - Containerized: `docker run --rm -e AWS_PROFILE -v "$HOME/.aws":/root/.aws amazon/aws-cli sts get-caller-identity` ### Default Gate Policy - min coverage: non-prod smoke validation for S3, SQS, SNS, secrets, and logging integration before promotion - max criticals: 0 for IAM and config findings - fail conditions: resources outside AWS EU region, missing encryption, missing trace or log sinks, cross-region data movement ### Enterprise Runner Notes - SonarQube: not primary for AWS validation, use it only for attached code quality data - Jenkins: optional enterprise wrapper, but cloud deployment evidence should still originate from the canonical pipeline - artifact flow: retain task definitions, image digests, deployment manifests, and smoke promoted images in AWS ECR and prefer mirrored dependencies for restricted environments - tokens: use federated AWS credentials or short-lived role assumption, never static keys in code or CI logs -
